ctes.order_classification:
SELECT
    COALESCE(S.ShipperID, O.ShipperID) AS ShipperID,
    COALESCE(S.CompanyName, 'Unknown shipper') AS shipper_name,
    CASE
        WHEN O.DeliveryDate IS NOT NULL
         AND NOT (
             O.OrderDate IS NOT NULL
             AND O.ShipDate IS NOT NULL
             AND O.DeliveryDate IS NOT NULL
             AND NOT (O.OrderDate <= O.ShipDate AND O.ShipDate <= O.DeliveryDate)
         )
        THEN 1 ELSE 0
    END AS is_delivered,
    CASE
        WHEN O.OrderDate IS NOT NULL
         AND O.ShipDate IS NOT NULL
         AND O.DeliveryDate IS NOT NULL
         AND O.OrderDate <= O.ShipDate
         AND O.ShipDate <= O.DeliveryDate
         AND julianday(O.DeliveryDate) - julianday(O.OrderDate) > 7
        THEN 1 ELSE 0
    END AS is_late,
    CASE WHEN O.DeliveryDate IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS not_delivered,
    CASE
        WHEN O.OrderDate IS NOT NULL
         AND O.ShipDate IS NOT NULL
         AND O.DeliveryDate IS NOT NULL
         AND NOT (O.OrderDate <= O.ShipDate AND O.ShipDate <= O.DeliveryDate)
        THEN 1 ELSE 0
    END AS invalid_dates
FROM Shippers AS S
FULL OUTER JOIN Orders AS O ON S.ShipperID = O.ShipperID

steps.title: Start with the shipper population
steps.change: Shippers is the first FROM source because the report must retain every registered shipper, including a shipper with no orders. Its three master rows define that population; the order source is added next to attach activity and reveal unknown IDs.

steps.title: Add every order without losing unmatched shippers
steps.change: Orders is added second because Orders.ShipperID is the available relationship key. FULL OUTER JOIN is necessary for both populations: NoOrders survives with NULL order fields, while order IDs 99 and NULL survive with NULL shipper fields. FastShip repeats once per matching order. This is a necessary relationship, not an interchangeable lookup.
steps.added_sql:
FULL OUTER JOIN Orders AS O
    ON S.ShipperID = O.ShipperID
steps.sql:
SELECT S.ShipperID AS shipper_id, S.CompanyName,
       O.OrderID, O.ShipperID AS order_shipper_id,
       O.OrderDate, O.ShipDate, O.DeliveryDate
FROM Shippers AS S
FULL OUTER JOIN Orders AS O ON S.ShipperID = O.ShipperID
ORDER BY COALESCE(S.ShipperID, O.ShipperID), O.OrderID;

steps.title: Classify each joined shipper/order row
steps.change: The CTE prepares one row per FULL OUTER JOIN result, not one row per shipper. It resolves the ID and label and computes four 0/1 flags from the order dates. The unmatched NoOrders row has zero flags; order 6 and order 7 both receive the Unknown shipper label.
steps.added_sql:
order_classification AS (...)
SELECT ShipperID, shipper_name, is_delivered, is_late,
       not_delivered, invalid_dates
FROM order_classification
steps.sql:
SELECT ShipperID, shipper_name, is_delivered, is_late,
       not_delivered, invalid_dates
FROM order_classification
ORDER BY ShipperID, shipper_name;

steps.title: Collapse classified rows into shipper groups
steps.change: The outer query groups the nine classified rows by resolved ShipperID and shipper_name. FastShip's four orders become one group; the two unmatched orders become one Unknown group; QuickShip and NoOrders each remain one group. SUM adds the row-level flags. NoOrders has zero delivered rows, so its delivered total is zero.
steps.added_sql:
SUM(is_delivered), SUM(is_late),
SUM(not_delivered), SUM(invalid_dates)
GROUP BY ShipperID, shipper_name
steps.sql:
SELECT ShipperID, shipper_name,
       SUM(is_delivered) AS delivered_orders,
       SUM(is_late) AS late_orders,
       SUM(not_delivered) AS not_delivered,
       SUM(invalid_dates) AS invalid_dates
FROM order_classification
GROUP BY ShipperID, shipper_name
ORDER BY ShipperID;

steps.title: Calculate the rate and sort the report
steps.change: The final stage is the exact saved learner query. Each group's late count is divided by its delivered count; NULLIF makes the zero-order shipper's rate NULL rather than dividing by zero. The four groups remain. The zero-order shipper's 0/0 classification is a known defect in the locked query's business interpretation and is deliberately preserved, not silently corrected.
steps.added_sql:
ROUND(SUM(is_late) * 100.0 /
      NULLIF(SUM(is_delivered), 0), 2)
ORDER BY late_rate_pct DESC
